questions.solution:
• Bimbisara was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty and ruled from 544 - 492 BCE.

• According to Ashvaghosha's Buddhacharita, Bimbisara belonged to the Haryanka dynasty and is considered the first important ruler of Magadha.

• Ajatashatru was Bimbisara's son who imprisoned and succeeded him.

• Mahapadma Nanda belonged to the Nanda dynasty which came much later.

• Udayin was a successor of Ajatashatru in the Haryanka dynasty.

• Initially, Rajagaha (the Prakrit name for present-day Rajgir in Bihar) was the capital of Magadha.

• Interestingly, the old name means "house of the king".

• Rajagaha was a fortified settlement, located amongst hills.

• Later, in the fourth century BCE, the capital was shifted to Pataliputra, present-day Patna, commanding routes of communication along the Ganga.

• Rajagriha (Girivraja) was the earliest capital of Magadha, surrounded by five hills that made it impregnable.

• Champa was the capital of the kingdom of Anga, not Magadha.

• Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji confederacy, a rival of Magadha.

questions.solution:
• Between the sixth and the fourth centuries BCE, Magadha (in present-day Bihar) became the most powerful mahajanapada.

• Modern historians explain this development in a variety of ways:

o Magadha was a region where agriculture was especially productive.

o Besides, iron mines (in present-day Jharkhand) were accessible and provided resources for tools and weapons.

o Elephants, an important component of the army, were found in forests in the region.

o Also, the Ganga and its tributaries provided a means of cheap and convenient communication.

o However, early Buddhist and Jaina writers who wrote about Magadha attributed its power to the policies of individuals: ruthlessly ambitious kings of whom Bimbisara, Ajatasattu and Mahapadma Nanda are the best known, and their ministers, who helped implement their policies.

Ajatashatru defeated the Vajji confederacy after a long war of sixteen years through deceit by sowing seeds of dissension with the help of his minister Vassakara. Bimbisara had cordial relations with neighboring states through marriage alliances. Udayin extended territories but did not defeat the Vajji confederacy.

Mahapadma Nanda came to power much later after the Vajji confederacy had already been defeated.

questions.solution:
Bimbisara (544 - 492 BCE) → Established marriage alliance with Kosala

• Bimbisara was one of the most powerful rulers of the Haryanka dynasty in Magadha.

• He expanded his empire through diplomatic marriages, one of which was with Kosala Devi, the princess of the Kosala kingdom.

• This marriage gave him control over Kashi as a dowry, strengthening Magadha's position.

• He also formed alliances with Vaishali and Madhura through similar strategies.

Ajatashatru (492 - 460 BCE) → Defeated Vajji confederacy

• Ajatashatru, the son of Bimbisara, fought against the Vajji confederacy, which had its capital at Vaishali.

• He used new war technologies like the rathamusala (chariot with rotating blades) and mahashilakantaka (catapult-like stone thrower).

• After years of warfare, he finally conquered Vajji, making Magadha even more powerful.

• He is also known for his interactions with Buddha and Mahavira, the founders of Buddhism and Jainism.

Udayin (460 - 444 BCE) → Shifted capital to Pataliputra

• Udayin, the son of Ajatashatru, is known for shifting the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha (modern Rajgir) to Pataliputra (modern Patna).

• He recognized the strategic advantage of Pataliputra, located at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers, making it easier to defend and trade.

• This move laid the foundation for Pataliputra becoming the political center of India for centuries.

Mahapadma Nanda (c. 4th century BCE) → Described as "exterminator of all kshatriyas"

• Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty, which succeeded the Haryanka dynasty.

• He was known for his aggressive expansionist policies and is often described as "Sarva-Kshatrantaka" (exterminator of all Kshatriyas).

• He overthrew many ruling Kshatriya dynasties to establish his dominance.

• Under his rule, Magadha became a large and powerful empire, setting the stage for the Mauryan Empire.

questions.solution:
• Mahashilakantaka (a large catapult for hurling rocks) and Rathamusala (a chariot fitted with a mace) were weapons that gave Magadha superior military technology.

• Jaladurga refers to a water fort, which was a defensive feature of Pataliputra, not a weapon.

• Girivraja was the ancient name of Rajagriha, the first capital of Magadha, not a weapon.

• The correct chronological order is Haryanka - Shishunaga - Nanda - Maurya.

• Bimbisara and Ajatashatru belonged to the Haryanka dynasty.

• Shishunaga dynasty followed when Shishunaga, a viceroy at Benaras, was placed on the throne in 413 BCE.

• The Nanda dynasty headed by Mahapadma Nanda followed the Shishunagas.

• The Mauryas came to power when Chandragupta overthrew the last Nanda king around 321 BCE.

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of the Haryanka dynasty? हर्यक वंश का अंतिम शासक कौन था?
questions.solution:
• Udayin, the son of Ajatashatru, was the last powerful ruler of the Haryanka dynasty.

• He was killed by his own ministers, leading to the rise of the Shishunaga dynasty.

• Kalashoka (Kakavarna), the successor of Shishunaga, presided over the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali in 383 BCE.

• This council led to the division of Buddhism into Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas.

• He was known for his immense wealth but was unpopular due to heavy taxation.

• Bimbisara (544 - 492 BCE) was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty and ruled from Rajgir.

• He formed marriage alliances with powerful kingdoms:

• Kosala (married Kosaladevi, sister of King Prasenajit)

• Vaishali (married Chellana, a Licchavi princess)

• Madra (married Khema, a Madra princess)

• Ajatashatru developed new war machines to defeat the Vajji confederacy.

• He used:

• Mahashilakantaka (a catapult-like device that hurled large stones).

• Rathamusala (a chariot with rotating blades).

• Kalashoka (also known as Kakavarna) was the last ruler of the Shishunaga dynasty.

• He was killed by Mahapadma Nanda, leading to the rise of the Nanda dynasty.

questions.solution:
• Dhana Nanda was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty and was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya.

• He was not defeated by Alexander - Alexander's army did not invade Magadha, as they turned back at the Beas River.

• The capital of Magadha during the Haryanka dynasty was Rajgir (earlier called Girivraja).

• It was later shifted to Pataliputra by Udayin, the last Haryanka ruler.

• Mahapadma Nanda overthrew the last Shishunaga ruler and established the Nanda dynasty.

• He centralized power and eliminated many Kshatriya dynasties, earning the title "Sarva-Kshatrantaka".

• Pushyamitra Shunga was NOT a ruler of Magadha during its earlier dynasties.

• He founded the Shunga dynasty after overthrowing the Mauryas in 185 BCE.
